newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, Korea to cooperate on cellphone standard.
newsitem.headline: Japan, Korea to cooperate on cellphone standard.

text.p: Japan and South Korea are to work together on next-generation cellular phones, a project which among other things will make it easier for them to host the 2002 soccer World Cup, a Japanese official said on Tuesday.
At present, mobile phone users in different countries cannot make calls to each other because each uses different frequencies and systems.

Japan has stepped up development of next-generation cellular phone technology and has been seeking allies in Asia because the U.N's International Telecommunication Union is due to decide on a single global cellular phone standard in 1999.

An official from Tokyo's Posts and Telecommunications Ministry said Japan and South Korea had agreed to exchange technology in an effort to establish the new world standard. He said the cooperation would allow them to use the same system during the 2002 World Cup, which they are to host jointly.
The United States and European countries are expected to propose rival standards.
To push its bid, Japan plans to hold a seminar on cellular phone technology in Beijing on December 13.
Japanese telecoms giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp developed a cellphone system in 1979 but failed to push the know-how internationally.
